title: CS Intake Orchestrator (aggregation + 10-minute scoping assistant)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Sales and Customer Success receive many enterprise feature asks that are scoped as separate notes across Slack, Zendesk, and email. This creates duplicated intake, inconsistent prioritization, and slow handoffs to Product/Eng. Goal: ship a lightweight CS Intake Orchestrator that provides (1) reliable aggregation/deduping across channels, (2) a short guided 10-minute scoping assistant for CS to capture the minimum necessary signal (customer need, success criteria, rough econ, urgency, desired deployment), and (3) an automatically generated first-pass scoping card for PMs and Eng (dev points, infra risk, suggested release track). This ticket covers the product definition, success metrics, and the initial implementation plan for the first MVP (CS Slack modal + intake aggregator + PM scoping card).
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator ingests requests from Slack thread, Zendesk ticket, and manual CS form and groups duplicate/near-duplicate asks into a single candidate card

CS can complete the 10-minute scoping assistant via Slack modal or quick web form; required fields: customer, business outcome, example prompt/workflow, estimated monthly usage, required confidentiality/regulatory constraints
System produces a PM scoping card with suggested engineering estimate (T-shirt + points), a one-line infra cost risk note, and a recommended release track (hosted/dedicated/private)
PM scoping cards appear in the Enterprise Intake board with flags for high econ impact or security/regulatory needs
Telemetry captures time-to-first-scope, aggregation rate, duplication reduction, and downstream conversion (percent of scoped asks that enter roadmap review)
CS team adoption pilot with 3 accounts over 2 weeks shows at least 50% faster handoffs (subjective CS report) and fewer duplicate tickets
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after discovery workshop with Sales and CS (Aisha). Key pain points documented: duplicates across channels, missing econ signal, slow PM handoffs.
2026-03-03: Scoped MVP with Eng and Design. Agreed to focus on Slack modal + lightweight web form for first release. Decided to postpone Zendesk connector to v1.1 to reduce scope.

2026-03-05: Design mocked up two modal flows: 'Quick ask' (5 fields) and 'Full scoper' (10 fields). Design feedback: avoid asking for engineering estimates from CS; system should auto-suggest estimates instead.
2026-03-07: Eng spike (ENG-22468) started to evaluate duplicate detection approaches. Initial approach: approximate text similarity (embedding + cluster) + explicit customer+feature matching.
2026-03-09: Privacy note: fields for 'regulatory constraints' flagged for secure storage; flagged to Security for compliance review but not blocking MVP (security_review_required=false).

2026-03-11: PM/Design review — approved MVP flows with minor copy edits; Eng raised concern about false-positive merging for multi-account features; agreed to keep a non-destructive 'group suggestion' step so CS can confirm aggregation.
2026-03-12: Implementation kickoff. Miguel to coordinate sprint tasks; initial frontend PR opened (see links). Planning pilot with East Coast CS pod (3 reps) starting 2026-03-17.
decisions: MVP will support Slack modal + quick web form; Zendesk/Email ingestion deferred to v1.1
Aggregation will be suggestion-based (group proposals) — never auto-merge without CS confirmation
Engineering estimate will be auto-suggested via rule-based heuristic (size buckets) and a 'confidence' score; final estimate set by PM
Release track recommendation will be based on required data isolation, expected rate, and SLA flagged by CS (rules defined in PRD)
Sensitive regulatory flags will be stored in encrypted fields and surfaced to PM/Legal but not included in public dashboards
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggregation causes unrelated feature requests to be combined -> Mitigation: present grouping suggestions with 'confirm' UX and show contributing excerpts
Risk: CS adoption low because additional friction -> Mitigation: keep quick flow < 5 fields and integrate into existing Slack workflows; provide credit for completion in CS onboarding
Risk: False econ signal causing prioritization noise -> Mitigation: require CS to include at least one business metric or customer quote; show historical usage benchmarks for similar asks
Risk: Sensitive data in freeform text -> Mitigation: redact PII client-side and store secure fields with KMS (ENG task for secure storage)
Risk: Slack rate limits for modal usage -> Mitigation: batch submissions and fallback to web form
